text:
Fraser Minten is 22, in his first full season as a Bruins regular after the trade from Toronto, and his line reads like a middle-six forward finding his feet: 7 goals and 13 points in 22 games on 16 minutes. He scored on the power play against Minnesota on Nov. 14, and Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub wrote afterward that he'd put Minten and David Pastrnak back together at five on five.

The underlying numbers are less settled. Boston has scored about seven goals more than its chances with him on the ice, and the team is more than seven points worse in expected-goal share with him than without him. His own finishing is also ahead of his chances (7 goals on 5.0 expected). His last ten games, with three points, are closer to what the chances say.

The skills are real. He has a heavy shot (90th percentile by speed) and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season. Watch whether his five-on-five share climbs as Boston settles its lines, because the on-ice luck won't last forever.
